title: Host API GPU drain playbook and graceful request amnesty
creator: Asha Patel
description: After the Feb capacity exhaustion incident, we need an operational playbook and code changes to allow GPU pools to drain gracefully while reducing queue amplification. This ticket captures an integrated plan: a scripted capacity-drain runbook, an admission-layer "request amnesty" path for short low-cost requests, soft-resume for tenants ejected by eviction, and autoscaler tuning to avoid oscillation. Goal: reduce tail latency and 5xx rate during pool drain events and allow controlled overflow handling without mass eviction.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Asha Patel: Summarized the incident postmortem and opened this ticket to track the large-scope mitigation. Link to postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/2025-02-gpu-exhaustion

2025-02-20 - Marcelo Ruiz: Spike complete. Proved that short requests (< 50 tokens / embeddings) can be fast-pathed through an optimistic admission channel with <10% additional CPU cost. Bench notes: /docs/bench/fastpath-2025-02-20.md
2025-02-24 - SRE rotation (K. Nguyen): Added runbook draft for controlled drain and tenant amnesty. Runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/412

2025-02-26 - Product (L. Gomez): Confirmed we can expose temporary reduction of per-tenant concurrency as config; requested telemetry to show number of amnesty decisions per tenant for 30 days before GA.

2025-03-01 - Marcelo Ruiz: Implemented admission-layer prototype in front of queue router. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/981, includes feature flag runtime.feature.fast_amnesty

2025-03-02 - QA (R. Singh): Smoke tested on staging with synthetic traffic (mix of short chat prompts + long completions). Observed 35% drop in queue depth during a simulated drain with fast-amnesty enabled. Logged detailed results: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/traffic/sim-2025-03-02
action_items: A1: Finalize drain runbook (SRE) - add checklist for pre-drain telemetry snapshot, drain start, eviction threshold, and post-drain validation - owner: K. Nguyen - due: 2025-03-05

A2: Harden admission controller to support 'amnesty' route for short requests (<50 tokens or single-embedding) with budgeted CPU allowance - owner: Marcelo Ruiz - implement behind FF - due: 2025-03-07
A3: Autoscaler hysteresis tuning - widen scale-down cooloff, add opportunistic pre-warm step to avoid cold-start spikes - owner: Platform Autoscale Team - due: 2025-03-10
A4: Telemetry additions - new metrics: amnesty_accept, amnesty_reject, drain_evicted_tenants, drain_queue_length_90p - owner: Observability (E. Park) - due: 2025-03-06
A5: Soft-resume mechanism - record last-eviction state and allow backfill at capped concurrency instead of full immediate restore - owner: Runtime (M. Ruiz) - due: 2025-03-12
A6: Canary rollout plan and guardrails - 10% traffic, 4-hour observation window; auto-rollback on >2x baseline 5xx or latency regression - owner: Release Eng - due: 2025-03-09
A7: Customer comms template for impacted tenants and support playbook - owner: Support (J. Adler) - due: 2025-03-08
A8: Post-implementation load test comparing current admission vs fast-amnesty under drain scenarios - owner: Performance Team - due: 2025-03-11
acceptance_criteria: AC1: During an orchestrated drain sim, queue depth 95p must be <= current baseline with <5% increase in CPU for control-plane components
AC2: Amnesty route accepts at least 70% of short requests under drain without increasing 5xx rate beyond baseline
AC3: Autoscaler must not oscillate (>=2 scale actions in 30m) during drain simulation
AC4: Runbook verified by on-call SRE in a dry-run and documented for on-call rotation
AC5: Metrics ingested into dashboards with 7d retention and alert thresholds configured
